key_insight: Additively manufactured porous wall lattices can delay hydrogen flame flashback, with the coarsest lattice giving the strongest improvement via wall cooling from mixture seepage.
engineering_relevance: Porous, 3D-printed nozzle walls offer a practical design lever for safer hydrogen combustors by improving flashback resistance without strongly altering the overall flow field.
method: Tested five combustor nozzle configurations with different wall lattice geometries.
Used pure hydrogen at atmospheric pressure over varying equivalence ratios and Reynolds numbers (9,000–12,000).
Combined flow-field measurements, flame imaging, and spectral proper orthogonal decomposition to track transition to flashback.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports only minor changes in flow and flame shape across configurations, but a coarser porous wall noticeably improved flashback resistance relative to a solid wall.
watch_item: The mitigation benefit appears tied to specific lattice porosity and cooling effects, so manufacturability, pressure drop, and durability must be validated before deployment.
paper_title: Effect of Additively Manufactured Wall Lattice Structures on Flashback Limits in a Hydrogen Jet Flame Combustor
